mainTopic: Sprinkling amounts, the status of a בכור's substitute and dedication, which offerings can get mixed up, and רבי שמעון on bringing קדשים to unfitness
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge. Rules saying that a הזאה of any amount purifies seem to show that רבי needs no minimum amount for placing blood. The גמרא answers that רבי was following רבי אליעזר, or that sprinkling water and placing blood are separate laws. Next, רמי בר חמא asks whether the תמורה of a blemished בכור keeps the בכור's restrictions, and רבא shows from a ברייתא that it does. רמי בר חמא then asks whether a בכור dedicated to בדק הבית may be sold by weight. After a proof and an objection are each knocked down, רבי אמי rules that a person can only give over what he owns, so it may not be sold by weight. The גמרא then explains which offerings can get mixed up: hair versus wool keeps a חטאת apart from an אשם, but age differences do not. A new משנה records רבי שמעון's view that a mixed אשם and שלמים are eaten by the stricter rules, and the חכמים object that holy food may not be brought to unfitness. The amud ends as רבה limits רבי שמעון's view to בדיעבד, and אביי begins an objection that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Challenge from the rule that any amount of sprinkling purifies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a challenge by quoting rules that a הזאה of any amount purifies, needs no minimum measure, and works even if half the water is unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: A sprinkling of any amount purifies. Sprinkling does not need a minimum measure. A sprinkling that is half fit and half unfit still works!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge that started just before this point. It quotes rules saying that sprinkling purification water works with any amount at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי holds that a tiny or mixed sprinkling of water works, it seems he should also hold that placing blood on the מזבח needs no minimum amount. That clashes with the view the גמרא was just discussing, that a minimum amount is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling, here of the purification water on someone who became impure
Any amount at all, even a tiny bit
A minimum required measure
Fit / unfit

phrases.english: A sprinkling of any amount purifies;
phrases.notes: This means sprinkling the purification water on someone who became impure from a dead body.

phrases.english: sprinkling does not require a minimum measure;
a sprinkling that is half fit and half unfit [still purifies]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge begun before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that placing blood needs a minimum amount
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If any amount of sprinkled water, even a mix of fit and unfit, purifies, then רבי seems to hold no minimum is needed, and blood should be the same.

steps.title: רבי was speaking according to רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי said this rule only according to רבי אליעזר's opinion, not his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said it according to the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying this ruling does not show what רבי himself thinks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי was explaining how things work within רבי אליעזר's view. So the quoted rule cannot be used to show that רבי himself holds no minimum is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the words (opinion) of someone else
He is saying

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume every ruling a תנא says is his own view. Sometimes he is just explaining someone else's position.

phrases.english: He stated it according to the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution: the statement reflects another תנא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule about sprinkling reflects רבי's own opinion
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי was only following רבי אליעזר's opinion, so his own view is not contradicted

steps.title: Sprinkling water and placing blood are separate laws
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: הזאה of water and נתינה of blood are two separate laws, so one tells us nothing about the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: sprinkling is one thing and placing blood is another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the same challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if רבי holds that any amount of sprinkled water works, that is a rule about water. Placing blood on the מזבח is a different law and can still need a minimum amount.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say instead (introduces another answer)
Placing, here of blood on the מזבח
Separate, by itself

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers: (1) רבי was speaking according to רבי אליעזר; (2) sprinkling water and placing blood are separate laws.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
sprinkling is separate and placement is separate.
phrases.notes: In other words, sprinkling the purification water and placing blood on the מזבח follow different rules.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to step 1
steps.terutzHavaAmina: What applies to sprinkling water applies to placing blood
steps.terutzMaskana: They are separate laws, so there is no contradiction

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about animals mixed with a בכור or מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new topic by quoting the משנה about offerings that became mixed up with a בכור or מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If they were mixed with a בכור or מעשר, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes the start of the משנה to open a new discussion about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ruled that such mixed animals graze until they get a blemish and are then eaten under the rules of a בכור or מעשר. That means they are not sold in the market or by weight. The next steps ask how far these rules reach.

keyTerms.meaning: They became mixed up
A firstborn animal, which is holy and given to a כהן
Animal tithe, every tenth animal
Etc.; the rest of the quote is left out

phrases.english: If they were intermingled with a firstborn or tithe, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals mixed with a בכור or מעשר are eaten under the rules of a בכור or מעשר once blemished

steps.title: Can the substitute of a בכור be fed to נדות?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks: according to בית שמאי, a בכור cannot be fed to נדות. Does the same apply to its תמורה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: according to בית שמאי, a בכור may not be fed to women who are נדות. What about its substitute?
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא asks whether a special restriction on a בכור also applies to an animal made into its substitute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי hold that even a blemished בכור keeps enough holiness that it may not be eaten by someone impure, like a נדה. The question is whether the תמורה, which got its holiness only through being exchanged, has that same strict status.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of שמאי
We feed (to others)
Women in a state of נדה impurity
A substitute animal that becomes holy by being exchanged for a holy one
What is the law?

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama says:
A firstborn, according to Beit Shammai,
one may not feed it to menstruating women;
what is the law of its substitute?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a question about the rules of a בכור mentioned in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the תמורה of a בכור is restricted from being fed to נדות, according to בית שמאי

steps.title: Can the substitute be redeemed or sold by weight?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks two more questions: a בכור cannot be redeemed or sold by the ליטרא, so what about its תמורה?
steps.simpleTranslation: A בכור cannot be redeemed; what about its substitute? A בכור cannot be weighed and sold by the pound; what about its substitute?
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא continues with two more questions of the same kind about the substitute of a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished בכור still cannot be redeemed, and its meat cannot be sold by weight like ordinary meat. All three questions ask one thing: does the תמורה carry the same special restrictions as the בכור itself?

keyTerms.meaning: Redeemed, made ordinary by paying money
Weighed
A unit of weight, like a pound

phrases.english: A firstborn may not be redeemed;
what is the law of its substitute?
A firstborn may not be weighed by the litra;
what is the law of its substitute?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds two more questions in the same pattern as step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the תמורה of a בכור can be redeemed or sold by weight

steps.title: רבא: the substitute has the same status as the original
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers from a ברייתא: once a בכור or מעשר is blemished, it can create a תמורה, and the תמורה is just like the original.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: a ברייתא teaches: a בכור or מעשר, once they have a blemish, can make a substitute, and their substitute is just like them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers all of רמי בר חמא's questions by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the תמורה of a blemished בכור or מעשר is 'like them.' So every restriction asked about carries over: no feeding to נדות (for בית שמאי), no redemption, and no selling by weight.

keyTerms.meaning: From when they got a blemish
They can create a substitute
Like them, with the same status

steps.whatToRemember: The תמורה of a blemished בכור or מעשר has exactly the same rules as the original animal.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the rule that a substitute takes on the full status of the animal it replaced, including its restrictions.

phrases.english: Rava says: It is taught in a baraita:
A firstborn or tithe, from when they become blemished,
they can render a substitute,
and their substitute is like them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the questions of steps 5 and 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תמורה has the same status and restrictions as the blemished בכור or מעשר

steps.title: Can a firstborn dedicated to the Temple be sold by weight?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks: if a בכור was dedicated to בדק הבית, may its meat be weighed by the ליטרא? Is the Temple's profit more important, or is avoiding disgrace to the בכור more important?
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked: If someone dedicated a firstborn animal to the upkeep of the Temple, may it be weighed and sold by the ליטרא? Is the Temple's profit more important, or is avoiding disgrace to the firstborn more important?
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא asks a new question. Normally a בכור may not be sold by weight, but what happens if selling it by weight would earn more money for the Temple?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling meat by exact weight makes the sale look like ordinary butcher meat, which is a disgrace to a holy בכור. But meat sold by weight brings a higher price, and here that money goes to הקדש. So two values pull against each other: more money for הקדש, or more respect for the בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: He dedicated (attached a holiness or vow to something)
The fund for upkeep and repair of the בית המקדש
The profit of the Temple treasury
Disgrace, treating something holy cheaply

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama asked:
If one dedicated a firstborn to the Temple upkeep fund,
phrases.notes: He means the כהן who got the בכור promised its value to the Temple.

phrases.english: may he weigh it out by the litra?
Is the profit of the Temple treasury more important,
or perhaps the disgrace of the firstborn is more important?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another question by רמי בר חמא about the בכור's rules, this time when the בכור has been dedicated to בדק הבית.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the ban on weighing a בכור by the ליטרא still hold when the profit goes to הקדש?

steps.title: Proof from the משנה about mixed-up offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר זבידא brings proof from the משנה: offerings mixed with a בכור are eaten like a בכור. That seems to mean they are not weighed by the ליטרא, even though there is a loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר זבידא said: Come and hear. If offerings got mixed up with a firstborn or with מעשר, they graze until they get a blemish and are then eaten like a firstborn or like מעשר. Doesn't that mean the other offering is also not weighed by the ליטרא?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר זבידא tries to answer the question using the משנה quoted earlier. He argues that the disgrace of the בכור wins out over the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the other offering could have been sold by weight for more money if it were alone. Yet because it is mixed with a בכור, it is treated like a בכור and not sold by weight. So avoiding disgrace to the בכור beats financial gain, and the same should apply to הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: They became mixed up
They graze until they get a blemish and become unfit for the מזבח
Meaning to say, implying

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר זְבִידָא, תָּא שְׁמַע:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Zevida said: Come and hear:
If offerings were mixed up with a firstborn or with tithe animals,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה quoted in step 4.

phrases.english: they graze until they become blemished,
and they are eaten like a firstborn or like tithe.
Doesn't this mean it is not weighed by the litra?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר זְבִידָא, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer רמי בר חמא's question from step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That the disgrace of the בכור outweighs financial gain, so a dedicated בכור is not weighed by the ליטרא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about offerings mixed up with a בכור or מעשר, which are eaten like a בכור.

steps.title: Two animals are different from one animal
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא and רבי חזקיה reject the proof. In the משנה there are two holinesses in two separate animals, but here both holinesses are in the same one animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא and רבי חזקיה, students of רבי ירמיה, said: Are these cases alike? There, there are two holinesses and two bodies. Here, there are two holinesses in one body.
steps.whatsHappening: Two students of רבי ירמיה push back on the proof. They say the משנה's case is not like our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the other offering is a separate animal, so its money interest cannot cause disgrace to a different animal that is a בכור. But when the בכור itself was dedicated to בדק הבית, the holiness of הקדש lives in the very same animal. So here הקדש's profit may be strong enough to allow weighing.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they alike? (a way of rejecting a comparison)
Holinesses, kinds of sanctity
Bodies, separate animals
There / here: comparing the two cases

phrases.english: Rav Huna and Rabbi Chizkiya,
students of Rabbi Yirmeya, said:
Are the cases alike?!
There, there are two holinesses and two bodies,
phrases.notes: The בכור is one animal and the mixed-in offering is a different animal.

phrases.english: here, there are two holinesses and one body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה, not necessarily the conclusion.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה deals with two separate animals, while our case has both holinesses in one animal, so the משנה tells us nothing here.

steps.title: One animal does not cancel the firstborn's rules
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין objects: if someone asked to redeem a בכור he dedicated to בדק הבית, surely we would not listen. So the one-animal idea does not cancel the rules of a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר אבין objected: What if he said, 'Redeem for me a firstborn that I dedicated to the Temple upkeep'? Would anyone listen to him?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר אבין challenges the distinction just made. He argues that a בכור keeps its own rules even when הקדש is in the same animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the הקדש holiness in the same animal could override the בכור's rules, then we should let him redeem it, which is obviously not allowed. So the בכור's own limits stay in force, and the ban on weighing should stay too.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it, raised a strong challenge
Redeem (exchange the holiness onto money)
Would we listen to him at all?

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin objected to this:
What if he said:
'Redeem for me a firstborn
that he dedicated to the Temple upkeep fund' —
would we listen to him at all?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'one body' distinction from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that הקדש's holiness in the same animal can override the בכור's rules.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even in one body we would never allow redeeming the בכור, so the בכור's rules are not overridden. Weighing should stay forbidden too.

steps.title: Redeeming is different: the Torah forbids it directly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the objection. Redeeming a בכור is forbidden by an explicit פסוק, 'do not redeem', so it cannot teach us about weighing by the ליטרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Redeem'?! The Torah says, 'You shall not redeem'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי יוסי בר אבין's objection. Redeeming is a special case because the Torah clearly forbids it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No profit to הקדש can override a direct Torah prohibition like 'לא תפדה'. But weighing by the ליטרא is not forbidden by the Torah, so in that case the profit of הקדש may still win. The comparison falls apart, and the next step gives a fresh answer to רמי בר חמא's question.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
You shall not redeem

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this step decides the halacha. It only knocks down רבי יוסי בר אבין's comparison. It does not prove that weighing is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows an important difference: a profit for הקדש cannot override an explicit Torah ban, but it may override a lesser rule like not weighing.

phrases.english: 'Redeem'?!
The Merciful One said: 'You shall not redeem'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between redeeming and weighing.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Redeeming a בכור is forbidden by an explicit פסוק, but weighing is not, so one cannot be learned from the other.

steps.title: A person can only give what he owns
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי answers רמי בר חמא: the giver can only pass on what belongs to him, so בדק הבית may not weigh the בכור's meat by the ליטרא either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אמי said: Can this person give over anything more than what belongs to him?
steps.whatsHappening: After the earlier proofs fell apart, רבי אמי gives a new answer to רמי בר חמא's question from Step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The giver himself was never allowed to sell the בכור's meat by weight. When he gives the animal to בדק הבית, he can only hand over the rights he actually had. So בדק הבית gets the animal with the same limit, and its meat may not be weighed by the ליטרא.

keyTerms.meaning: handed over ownership; gave over
belongs to him; is his to own
used here as a question: 'can he really…?'

steps.whatToRemember: A person cannot give away more rights than he has. בדק הבית receives the בכור with all the limits the giver had, so its meat is not weighed by the ליטרא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer closes רמי בר חמא's question, and it does so with a simple ownership rule instead of the comparisons that were knocked down in Steps 9-12.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Ami said:
Can this one hand over anything
other than what belongs to him?!
phrases.notes: Some versions say the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The proofs and objections ended without a decision, so the גמרא gives a fresh answer to the question from Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The meat is not weighed by the ליטרא, because בדק הבית only gets the rights the giver had.

steps.title: Why can't a חטאת and an אשם get mixed up?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and asks why only a חטאת and an אשם cannot be confused. It suggests the reason: an אשם is always male and a חטאת is always female.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'All offerings can get mixed up with each other, etc.' What is different about a חטאת and an אשם? Is it that this one is male and that one is female?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה and asks why a חטאת and an אשם are left out of the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says any two kinds of offerings could get mixed up, except a חטאת with an אשם. The גמרא offers a reason: a regular חטאת is a female animal and an אשם is a male animal, so anyone can tell them apart. The next steps test this suggested reason.

keyTerms.meaning: to get mixed up, so you cannot tell which animal is which
what is different about…?
sin offering; usually a female animal
guilt offering; always a male animal

phrases.english: 'All can become mixed up, etc.'
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה, which goes on to say: except a חטאת with an אשם.

phrases.english: What is different about a sin offering and a guilt offering?
Is it that this one is male and that one is female?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This begins a new section on the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a חטאת and an אשם can never be confused with each other.

steps.title: A חטאת and an עולה also differ in gender
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reason: a חטאת is female and an עולה is male too, so why doesn't the משנה say those two cannot get mixed up?
steps.simpleTranslation: A חטאת and an עולה should also not get mixed up!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the 'male and female' reason from Step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If male versus female is what keeps two offerings apart, then a חטאת (female) and an עולה (male) should also be impossible to confuse. Yet the משנה lists only חטאת and אשם as the exception.

keyTerms.meaning: burnt offering; a male animal
also

phrases.english: A sin offering and a burnt offering too!
phrases.notes: He means: these two should also be impossible to mix up, since one is female and one is male.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This tests the reason suggested in Step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reason would also rule out mixing a חטאת with an עולה, but the משנה does not say that.

steps.title: The נשיא's goat, and hair versus wool
steps.stepSummary: There is a male חטאת, the goat of the נשיא, which could get mixed up with a male goat brought as an עולה. But it can never be confused with an אשם, because a goat has hair and an אשם comes from sheep, which have wool.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is the goat of the נשיא. And this one has hair, while that one has wool.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and gives a new reason why a חטאת and an אשם stay apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every חטאת is female: the נשיא brings a male goat. So a חטאת can get mixed up with a male goat עולה. Since a male חטאת exists, gender alone cannot be the full reason. The real difference is the coat: a goat has hair, while an אשם is always a sheep or ram, which has wool, so the two always look different.

keyTerms.meaning: the male goat that a leader (נשיא) brings as his חטאת
hair, the coat of a goat
wool, the coat of a sheep

steps.confusionAlert: The answer has two parts. Part one explains why a חטאת and an עולה can mix (the נשיא's male goat). Part two explains why a חטאת and an אשם still cannot mix (hair versus wool).

phrases.english: There is the goat of the Nasi;
phrases.notes: This is a male חטאת, so it could get mixed up with a male goat עולה.

phrases.english: this one has hair and that one has wool.
phrases.notes: An אשם always comes from sheep, never goats.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the challenge from Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the reason: from male versus female to hair versus wool.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought gender was the reason, which would also keep a חטאת and an עולה apart.
steps.terutzMaskana: A male חטאת exists, so a חטאת can mix with an עולה. A חטאת and an אשם stay apart because of hair versus wool.

steps.title: A פסח and an אשם differ in age
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: a פסח is in its first year and an אשם is in its second year, so they should not get mixed up either.
steps.simpleTranslation: A פסח and an אשם also cannot get mixed up! This one is in its first year and that one is in its second year!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second challenge to the משנה's list of what can get mixed up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה implies that a פסח could get mixed up with an אשם. But a פסח is a young lamb in its first year, while an אשם is a ram in its second year. Their age difference should make them easy to tell apart.

keyTerms.meaning: the Pesach offering; must be in its first year
an animal in its first year
an animal in its second year

phrases.english: A Paschal offering and a guilt offering also cannot get mixed up –
this one is in its first year
and that one is in its second year!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a new challenge to the משנה's list of offerings that can get mixed up.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's implication that a פסח and an אשם can get mixed up.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their difference in age should keep them apart.

steps.title: Some אשם offerings are young lambs
steps.stepSummary: The אשם of a נזיר and the אשם of a מצורע are lambs in their first year, so they can get mixed up with a פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is the אשם of a נזיר and the אשם of a מצורע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing to kinds of אשם that are young lambs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every אשם is a two-year-old ram. The אשם of a נזיר and of a מצורע are first-year lambs, the same age as a פסח. So these can be confused with a פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: the guilt offering brought by a נזיר
the guilt offering brought by a מצורע when he becomes pure

phrases.english: There is the guilt offering of a nazirite
and the guilt offering of a leper.
phrases.notes: These two are lambs in their first year, the same age as a פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the challenge from Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to particular cases that fit the rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed every אשם is in its second year.
steps.terutzMaskana: Some kinds of אשם are first-year lambs and can get mixed up with a פסח.

steps.title: Ages can look alike
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: even a first-year and a second-year animal can be confused, because some young animals look older and some older animals look younger.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: there is a first-year animal that looks like a second-year one, and a second-year animal that looks like a first-year one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, separate answer to the challenge from Step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer does not need the נזיר or מצורע cases. Age is not something you can always see, unlike hair versus wool. So any פסח could get mixed up with any אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and if you want, say': brings a second answer
looks like

steps.whatToRemember: A חטאת and an אשם can never be confused because of hair versus wool, which you can always see. Age differences, such as a פסח versus an אשם, do not keep offerings apart.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא בֶּן שָׁנָה דְּמִיחֲזֵי כְּבֶן שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים,
phrases.english: there is a first-year animal that looks like a second-year one,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיכָּא בֶּן שְׁתַּיִם דְּמִיחֲזֵי כְּבֶן שָׁנָה.
phrases.english: and there is a second-year animal that looks like a first-year one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a second answer to Step 17's challenge, separate from the answer in Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the idea that age keeps animals apart.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An age difference always keeps two animals easy to tell apart.
steps.terutzMaskana: You cannot always tell age by looking, so animals of different ages can get mixed up.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: a mixed אשם and שלמים follow the stricter rules
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. רבי שמעון rules that if an אשם and a שלמים got mixed up, both are slaughtered in the north and both are eaten under the stricter rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If an אשם got mixed up with a שלמים, רבי שמעון says: both are slaughtered in the north, and both are eaten according to the stricter of the two.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. רבי שמעון gives his solution for a guilt offering that got mixed up with a peace offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם must be slaughtered in the northern part of the עזרה, but a שלמים may be slaughtered anywhere there, so slaughtering both in the north works for both. For eating, the אשם is stricter: only male כהנים may eat it, only inside the עזרה, and only for one day and a night. So רבי שמעון treats both animals like an אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt offering, one of the holiest offerings, slaughtered in the north
Peace offering, a lighter-holiness offering eaten for two days and a night
The northern part of the courtyard, where the holiest offerings are slaughtered
According to the stricter of the two

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A guilt offering that got mixed up with a peace offering:
Rabbi Shimon says:
Both of them should be slaughtered in the north,
and they should be eaten according to the stricter of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָשָׁם שֶׁנִּתְעָרֵב בִּשְׁלָמִים רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion of which animals can get mixed up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mixed אשם and שלמים are both slaughtered in the north and both eaten under the stricter rules of the אשם.

steps.title: The חכמים object: holy food may not be pushed toward unfitness
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject רבי שמעון's solution, because it makes the שלמים become forbidden earlier than it should.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: One may not bring holy offerings to a state of unfitness.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים argue with רבי שמעון. They say his plan harms the שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שלמים may normally be eaten for two days and a night. Under רבי שמעון's plan it may only be eaten for one day and a night, so whatever is left becomes נותר too early. The חכמים say you may not cause holy food to become unfit like that.

keyTerms.meaning: A state of being unfit (for example, leftover meat that must be burned)
Offering meat left past its allowed time, which must be burned
Holy offerings

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are not saying the mix-up has no solution. They object only to cutting down the שלמים's eating time; they have a different way to deal with the mixed animals.

phrases.english: They said to him:
phrases.notes: "They" are the חכמים who disagree with רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: One may not bring holy offerings to a state of unfitness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ אֵין מְבִיאִין קָדָשִׁים לְבֵית הַפְּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי שמעון's ruling in step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי שמעון's solution of eating both animals under the stricter rules.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His plan shortens the שלמים's eating time and causes it to become נותר too early.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that one may not bring holy things to unfitness, is what the גמרא goes on to explore.

steps.title: Mixed pieces of meat are eaten by the stricter rule
steps.stepSummary: If already-cut pieces of different offerings got mixed, everyone agrees they are eaten under the stricter offering's rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: If pieces got mixed with pieces, such as קדשי קדשים with קדשים קלים, or meat eaten for one day mixed with meat eaten for two days and a night, they are eaten according to the stricter of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a case where the stricter rule is used. Here the meat is already cut into pieces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With live animals, the חכמים have another option: wait until the animals get a blemish and then redeem them. Pieces of meat cannot be handled that way, so there is no choice but to eat everything by the stricter rule. This shows that even the חכמים agree when there is no other solution.

keyTerms.meaning: Pieces of meat
Offerings of the highest holiness (like אשם and חטאת)
Offerings of lighter holiness (like שלמים)

steps.whatToRemember: With mixed live animals, רבי שמעון and the חכמים argue. With mixed cut pieces, everyone agrees: eat by the stricter rule.

phrases.english: If pieces got mixed up with pieces:
offerings of the highest holiness with offerings of lighter holiness,
those eaten for one day
with those eaten for two days and a night:
they are eaten according to the stricter of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a case where the stricter-rule approach is accepted, unlike the dispute in steps 20-21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mixed pieces of offerings with different rules are eaten according to the stricter offering.

steps.title: A ברייתא: do not buy תרומה with שביעית money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא taught before רב: you may not use money from שביעית produce to buy תרומה, because that shortens the eating time.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A תנא taught before רב: With money from שביעית produce, one may not buy תרומה, because this shortens the time for eating it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting a ברייתא that uses the same idea as the חכמים: do not shorten the eating time of holy food. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money from selling שביעית produce takes on the holiness of שביעית, and whatever you buy with it may only be eaten until the time of ביעור. תרומה normally has no time limit. Buying תרומה with that money would give it a deadline, just like רבי שמעון's plan gave the שלמים an earlier deadline.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא (reciter of ברייתות) taught before רב
Produce of the seventh (Sabbatical) year, which has special holiness
The portion of produce given to a כהן
Shortening the time it may be eaten

phrases.english: GEMARA:
A reciter taught before Rav:
With the money of Sabbatical-year produce, one may not buy תרומה,
because one shortens the time for eating it.
phrases.notes: שביעית food may only be eaten until the time of ביעור, so the תרומה would pick up that deadline.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא with the same idea as the חכמים's rule in step 21, beginning the גמרא's discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not buy תרומה with שביעית money, because doing so shortens the time the תרומה may be eaten.

steps.title: The Sages say the ברייתא does not fit רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The scholars (רבנן) in רבה's study hall tell him that the ברייתא forbidding the use of שביעית money to buy תרומה does not match רבי שמעון. רבי שמעון says we may bring קדשים to a state of unfitness.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages said this ברייתא in front of רבה: 'This does not follow רבי שמעון. If it followed רבי שמעון, doesn't he say that we may bring holy things to a state of unfitness?'
steps.whatsHappening: Scholars speaking before רבה point out a clash between the ברייתא from step 23 and רבי שמעון's ruling in the משנה from step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי שמעון lets the שלמים be eaten under the stricter אשם rules. That shortens its eating time, so the leftover becomes forbidden sooner. The ברייתא forbids shortening the eating time of שביעית produce, so it seems to disagree with רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages said it in front of him
This does not follow (a certain opinion)
We may bring holy things to a state where they become unfit
A state of unfitness, such as becoming נותר

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון never says outright 'we may bring קדשים to unfitness.' The scholars before רבה are drawing this from his ruling about the mixed-up אשם and שלמים. They are not the חכמים of the משנה.

phrases.english: The Sages said it before
Rabba:
phrases.notes: Some versions say רבא, in round brackets. The corrected wording, in square brackets, is רבה.

phrases.english: This is not in line with Rabbi Shimon;
for if it were in line with Rabbi Shimon, doesn't he say:
We may bring holy things to a state of unfitness!
phrases.notes: This comes from step 20. Eating the שלמים by the stricter rules makes it go bad sooner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which תנא the ברייתא from step 23 follows
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the ברייתא could follow רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון allows shortening the eating time of קדשים. The ברייתא forbids shortening the eating time of שביעית. So the two seem to conflict.

steps.title: רבה: רבי שמעון allows it only after the fact
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the ברייתא can still follow רבי שמעון. רבי שמעון only allowed bringing קדשים to unfitness בדיעבד, not לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: You can even say it follows רבי שמעון. His rule applies only when it already happened, but not from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends the ברייתא by showing that it fits רבי שמעון after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה the animals were already mixed up, which is a בדיעבד situation. רבי שמעון only allows the shortened eating time there. Buying תרומה with שביעית money is a choice made from the start, so even רבי שמעון would forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: You may even say
This rule applies only
After the fact, once it already happened
From the start, as a first choice

steps.whyThisMatters: The difference between בדיעבד and לכתחילה is what reconciles the ברייתא with רבי שמעון. The next step tests this distinction.

phrases.english: He said to them:
You may even say it follows Rabbi Shimon –
that applies only after the fact,
but from the start, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 24
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון allows bringing קדשים to unfitness in every case, so he would disagree with the ברייתא
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון allows it only after the fact, so the ברייתא, which deals with a choice made from the start, fits him

steps.title: Is it really not allowed from the start? אביי objects
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבה's limit, and אביי begins to bring a source against it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from the start it is not allowed?! אביי raised an objection to him:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא doubts רבה's claim. This line sets up אביי's challenge, which comes from a משנה quoted next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said רבי שמעון never allows bringing קדשים to unfitness from the start. The גמרא is surprised by this and signals that a source shows רבי שמעון allows it even לכתחילה. The actual proof is quoted in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: אביי, a student of רבה

steps.confusionAlert: The proof itself does not appear yet. The colon after אביי's name means the source he quotes comes next.

phrases.english: And from the start, it is not allowed?!
Abaye raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבה, who just gave the answer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's answer from step 25
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that רבי שמעון does not allow bringing קדשים to unfitness לכתחילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה, quoted next, seems to show רבי שמעון allows it even from the start
